920: They booked our finest suite under a name I'm fairly sure they invented on the way in.
921: They took the grandest room we have and immediately asked why it wasn't grander.
922: They signed the register with a flourish and a name that had changed slightly by the elevator.
923: They demanded the best suite, toured it, and requested we find one that was somehow better.
924: They complained the chandelier was too small, the bed too ordinary, and the view insufficiently theirs.
925: They reserved the top floor under a false name and asked us to keep their real one a secret we never learned.
926: They wanted the finest suite and then a second one beside it, purely so no one could be near them.
927: They asked whether the grand suite was truly our grandest, and looked wounded when I confirmed it.
928: They booked the best room in the house and left it untouched, having only wanted to own it briefly.
929: They insisted the suite be redecorated at once, since no wall should be permitted to outshine its guest.
930: They arrived, disliked the lobby, disliked the suite, and adored themselves throughout.
931: They insisted the finest suite be aired out twice, as no ordinary air would do for them.
932: They demanded the royal suite, then asked if we had ever hosted anyone more important than them.
933: They booked under a false name so smooth I almost put it on a little plaque.
934: They requested our finest room and complained it lacked the one thing it needed: more of itself.
935: They swept in expecting the whole staff to already know their invented name.
936: They took the grand suite, rearranged the furniture, and left it grander than the hotel could afford.
937: They asked for the most expensive room and seemed disappointed we didn't have a costlier one hidden away.
938: They checked in under a name, complained about the towels, and checked out under quite another.
939: They demanded the presidential suite and asked, politely, whether we had anything above a president.
940: They handed me luggage so heavy my knees made a sound I had never heard before.
941: They gave me bags that clinked like a treasure chest and a tip that clinked even louder.
942: They asked me to carry everything at once, tipped me grandly, and were gone before I set it down.
943: They over-tipped me so severely I almost asked whether it was a mistake, then decided not to risk it.
944: They handed me a case I could barely lift and warned me, sweetly, not to shake it.
945: They tipped me before I lifted a single bag, which should have told me how heavy the bags were.
946: They had more luggage than a family of ten and insisted every piece was terribly fragile.
947: They pointed at a mountain of bags, called them their essentials, and vanished before I finished.
948: They set down a case, watched me strain to lift it, and looked quietly proud of how much it weighed.
949: They asked me to hurry with the bags, praised how quickly I moved, and were nowhere in sight by the time I finished.
950: They handed me a trunk that took two of us to lift and tipped as though it had taken ten.
951: They loaded my cart until the wheels complained, then rewarded me like I'd carried it up a mountain.
952: They tipped me, thanked me, praised me, and were simply not there when I turned around.
953: They insisted on carrying nothing themselves, not even the small bag that held only their gloves.
954: They handed me a bag heavy as an anchor and told me, cheerfully, it was mostly souvenirs.
955: They over-tipped me and asked me to forget how heavy the bags were, which I could not.
956: They gave me luggage that groaned when I picked it up and a tip that left me speechless.
957: They had me stack the bags just so, admired my work, tipped generously, and slipped away.
958: They handed me a case marked fragile that weighed more than the cart I put it on.
959: They tipped me twice, once for carrying the bags and once, they said, for my silence.
